Package neqsim.thermo.phase

Class PitzerMegParameters

java.lang.Object
neqsim.thermo.phase.PitzerMegParameters
public final class PitzerMegParameters extends Object
Neutral-solute Pitzer parameters for monoethylene glycol (MEG) in water and in aqueous NaCl.

MEG is treated as a neutral solute on the molality scale. For MEG alone, the osmotic coefficient of water is $\phi = 1 + \lambda m + 2\mu m^2$ and $\ln a_w = -M_w m \phi$, with $\lambda(T)$ and $\mu(T)$ in the PHREEQC six-term form referenced to 298.15 K. The binary parameters were regressed by NeqSim to the freezing points (233-269 K) and the 298.15 K isopiestic water activities of aqueous ethylene glycol reported by Tsurko et al. (2026), J. Chem. Eng. Data 71, 942-959 (Tables 2 and 44). The NaCl term was regressed to the ternary water/NaCl/ethylene-glycol melting-point equation of Benson et al. (2010), Cryobiology 61, 352-356, for EG:NaCl mass ratios 5-45 and total solute up to 30 wt% (rms 0.70 K in freezing temperature). Only the sum of the MEG-Na+ and MEG-Cl- lambda terms is identifiable from water-activity data of a single salt; by convention the full value is assigned to MEG-Na+ and the MEG-Cl- term is zero.

Qualified scope: MEG molality up to 17.6 mol/kg water (about 52 wt% salt-free), 233-298 K for the binary and 248-273 K for the NaCl term (NaCl up to 1.22 mol/kg in the regression data), with Na+ and Cl- as the only ions. Other cations (K+, Ca++, Mg++) have no MEG rows; the neutral coverage audit then fails with a diagnostic rather than assuming zero. MEG together with methanol or another liquid co-solvent likewise fails closed. Dilute molecular gases and hydrocarbons receive explicit zero rows with MEG, listed by PhasePitzer.getMegAssumedZeroRows(), which reproduces their ideal-dilute treatment.

    • henryReference

      public static double henryReference(ComponentInterface component, double temperature)
      Molality-scale Henry reference of MEG, bar kg/mol, from its pure-liquid vapour pressure.

      Uses the Raoult limit $H_m = M_w p^{sat}_{MEG}(T)$, i.e. a symmetric infinite-dilution activity coefficient of one. This sets only the small MEG volatility into gas and oil; it does not enter the water activity.

      Parameters:
      component - MEG component
      temperature - temperature in K
      Returns:
      Henry reference in bar kg/mol
